subject: Emotions
title: Shame and Suicide
description: A 60-second lesson on Shame and Suicide.

hook.text: Thomas Joiner's research found that shame—not sadness—is the strongest emotional predictor of suicidal thinking.

buildup.text: His theory identifies 'perceived burdensomeness'—the belief that you're a burden to others—as a core shame state.

discovery.text: Shame makes connection feel impossible: 'If they knew the real me, they'd leave.' Isolation follows, then despair.

twist.text: Public humiliation events—leaked photos, scandals, bullying—spike suicide risk because they weaponize shame.

climax.text: Suicide prevention requires shame reduction: making people feel they belong and matter before crisis hits.

punchline.text: People don't want to die. They want the shame to stop.

quiz.question: What does Thomas Joiner identify as a core predictor of suicidal thinking?
